title: Hymns of the Atharva-Veda (SBE 42)
altTitles: Sacred Books of the East, vol. 42
attributionNote: The hymns are anonymous. The selection, the translation and the explanatory notes are Maurice Bloomfield's, made for the Sacred Books of the East.
description: Bloomfield's selection presents the Atharvaveda by subject rather than in the order of the printed collection: charms against fever and disease, spells for the healing of wounds and for protection in battle, hymns to the plants and to the earth, the great speculative hymns on brahman, time, life-breath and the primordial power, and the funeral and marriage formulae. The full translation and notes of SBE 42 make the volume the scholarly counterpart to Griffith's complete text.
historicalContext: Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) was professor of Sanskrit at Johns Hopkins and one of the founders of Vedic philology in America. His translation appeared in 1897 as volume 42 of the Sacred Books of the East, with an introduction on the text and its religion and a body of notes drawing on the Kauśika Sutra and the commentary of Sayana.
availabilityNote: Complete as published: the selected hymns with translation and notes, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one hymn per chapter. This is Bloomfield's selection for SBE 42, not the whole twenty-book collection; the complete text is the Griffith translation in this library.
